# Delta expands Wi-Fi across Asia-Pacific routes, completing global connectivity map


With nearly 1,300 Wi-Fi-equipped aircraft and free global Wi-Fi presented by T-Mobile now available across Asia-Pacific routes, Delta now offers free connectivity across its full international network (spanning six continents) – the only U.S.-based carrier to do so. The expansion marks a major milestone in Delta’s connectivity journey, closing the final coverage gap and helping customers stay connected across some of the airline’s longest flights.


Staff Writer


Oct 20, 2026 7:00am


With nearly 1,300 Wi-Fi-equipped aircraft and the Pacific now connected, Delta customers can enjoy free global Wi-Fi presented by T-Mobile across the airline’s full international network. SkyMiles Members traveling to and from the Asia-Pacific region can now access Delta’s award-winning onboard connectivity, closing the last coverage gap and making the connected travel experience more available across Delta’s global network.


For customers working across time zones, staying in touch with colleagues, family or simply keeping up with what matters most to them, onboard connectivity has become an increasingly important part of the travel experience. With free global Wi‑Fi now available across Asia-Pacific routes, SkyMiles Members in all cabins can stay connected on some of Delta's longest flights. Once boarding doors close, customers can easily connect on one or more devices to message, email, browse, scroll, share photos and more — including streaming videos on their own devices, in their own languages.


***Not a SkyMiles Member yet?***[Join today for free.](https://www.delta.com/joinskymiles/) ******


“We know how important connectivity is for travelers who want to stay connected wherever they fly, whether you're traveling for business, reconnecting with family or setting out on a long-awaited trip,” said Ranjan Goswami, Chief Marketing and Product Officer. “Bringing free global Wi-Fi across our international network is an important milestone in making the Delta experience more consistent and connected, especially on some of our longest journeys."


“Completing Delta’s global Wi-Fi coverage is a major and meaningful milestone for our customers, especially as we grow to meet increased demand for travel across the Asia-Pacific region,” said Jeff Moomaw, Vice President – Asia Pacific. “Together with our partners, we’re making it easier for customers to stay connected as they travel across the Pacific and beyond.”


**Ready for your next Asia-Pacific adventure?** With free global Wi-Fi now available across Delta’s trans-Pacific routes, customers can stay connected from takeoff to touchdown — and start planning what comes next. Explore Delta’s destination guides for[Seoul](https://news.delta.com/destination/your-guide-seoul) and[Hong Kong](https://news.delta.com/your-guide-hong-kong) for travel inspiration, local highlights and tips to make the most of your journey.


The milestone also comes as new satellite capacity enters service across the Americas, which will further strengthen network capacity and support growing demand for reliable connectivity. Together with service expansion across Asia-Pacific, that added capacity helps support Delta’s broader goal of making onboard Wi-Fi feel more consistent wherever customers fly.


Delta operates one of the world’s largest connected fleets, with nearly 1,300 Wi-Fi-equipped aircraft—more than 95% of the airline’s fleet. Full fleet connectivity is expected by early 2027 as coverage extends to remaining Delta Connection regional jets and the narrowbody Boeing 717 fleet.


#### **Delta Sync: By the numbers**


- Nearly 1,300 Wi-Fi-equipped aircraft
- More than 95% of fleet equipped
- More than 195M Delta Sync Wi-Fi sessions logged since launching in 2023


### Wi-Fi and so much more: Exploring Delta Sync


Once logged in, Members can unlock a world of connected experiences and offers through Delta Sync — turning time in flight into time to be entertained, inspired, informed and treated. Delta Sync is designed to help customers do more with their journey, whether that means streaming premium entertainment and can’t-miss sports moments, catching up on news and ideas, staying connected to loved ones, or discovering benefits available through Delta Sync.


That matters especially on longer-haul routes, when customers have more time to choose how they want to spend their flight. Wi-Fi provides SkyMiles Members with fast, free connectivity, while the Delta Sync experience helps surface what else is included in the journey — from partner content and entertainment to relevant offers and information.


- **Stay informed** with award-winning journalism and insights from The New York Times and Wall Street Journal
- **Stay entertained** with streaming partners Crunchyroll and Paramount+*
- **Stay in the game** with Sport 24, Delta Sync’s partner for live-sports streaming


**Available to U.S.-based SkyMiles Members with flights originating from the U.S.*


With new partners added regularly, there’s always more to discover and explore through Delta Sync+.


Delta’s latest onboard partnership lets you stay connected to the world’s biggest sports moments – even when crossing time zones and oceans. With Sport 24, customers can access around-the-clock live sports programming, including major sports properties like the NFL, NBA, Formula 1, and Grand Slam tennis.


[On Board](https://news.delta.com/category/board)


[Game on: Delta takes sports fandom global with new Sport 24 partnership](https://news.delta.com/game-delta-takes-sports-fandom-global-new-sport-24-partnership)


Delta is teaming up with Sport 24, IMG’s dedicated live sports channel for the airline and cruise industries, to bring 24/7 live sports coverage to customers on international routes through Delta Sync Wi-Fi.


*+Listed partners represent offers available on international flights. Terms apply; read more on Delta Sync offerings*[here](https://www.delta.com/us/en/about-delta/sync) *.*


### How to connect


Getting online is easy – here’s how to connect in three steps:


1. Open your device settings on your electronic device
2. Turn on Airplane Mode, then turn your Wi-Fi on
3. Choose the DeltaWiFi.com network, then follow instructions on the portal to connect*


**If the Wi-Fi sign-in page does not open or if you see an error message, go to DeltaWiFi.com using your browser.*
